title: You Are What You Annotate: Towards Better Models through Annotator Representations
measurement_description: The paper evaluated annotator disagreement and the impact of annotator/annotation embeddings on classification tasks. In the context of religion, it specifically analyzed abusive language detection targeting Muslims (using the HS-Brexit dataset) to examine how the religious background of annotators (Muslim immigrants vs. non-Muslims) influenced their perception and annotation of hate speech regarding Islam and Muslims.
findings: The paper found that relying on a single demographic feature like religion is insufficient for predicting perceptions of hate speech. Specifically, annotators belonging to the same demographic group (e.g., Muslim immigrants in the UK) often held contrasting opinions and disagreed with each other on whether specific tweets about Islam constituted hate speech. This highlights the importance of modeling individual annotator idiosyncrasies rather than relying purely on group-level demographic identities.
